before.title: Bonneville 3800 V6 Lower Intake Manifold (LIM) Gasket Failure
before.description: 1995-2005 Bonneville with the 3800 Series II / III V6 (L36 NA or L67 supercharged) suffers the same LIM gasket failure that hit Buick Park Avenue/LeSabre, Olds 88, Chevy Monte Carlo, etc. Plastic intake material softens under coolant exposure (especially Dex-Cool); coolant migrates into the valley and oil. Catastrophic if undetected.
before.solution: Replace LIM gasket with updated Fel-Pro MS98003T (improved metal-reinforced) — $400-$800 at independent. Replace upper intake plenum if cracked. Drain Dex-Cool and refill with Zerex G-05. Check oil for coolant at every change.

milky oil
overheating
sweet exhaust
rough idle

cooling system

proposal.title: Bonneville 3800 V6 Lower Intake Manifold (LIM) Gasket Failure
proposal.description: The exact Bonneville communications support several bounded coolant-leak conditions, not the frozen eleven-year lower-intake-gasket identity. before.title: Crankshaft Position Sensor / Ignition Control Module Failure Causing Stalling and No-Start
before.description: Failing crankshaft position sensors and ignition control modules are among the most common causes of intermittent stalling and no-spark no-start conditions on 3800-powered Bonnevilles, documented by RepairPal as a known model problem. The CKP sensor's hall-effect elements degrade with heat, causing the engine to randomly die while driving — often with no trouble code — and frequently restart only after cooling down. The ICM, which needs both 18X and 3X/sync crank signals to fire the coils, exhibits the same heat-related intermittent failure.
before.solution: Test the crank sensor and ICM circuits and replace the failed component; the dual CKP sensor sits behind the harmonic balancer, so the crank pulley must be pulled, and a crank relearn may be required after replacement. Many high-mileage owners replace the CKP sensor and ICM together to end repeat intermittent stalls.
symptoms: Engine stalls randomly while driving
Restarts only after sitting and cooling down
Cranks but no start with no spark
Tachometer drops to zero before a stall
Check engine light may or may not illuminate

proposal.title: Crankshaft Position Sensor / Ignition Control Module Failure Causing Stalling and No-Start
proposal.description: The frozen page attributes intermittent stall and no-start conditions across 1992-2005 Bonneville to crankshaft-position-sensor and ignition-control-module heat failure. The exact corpus instead shows multiple bounded causes: record 39724 identifies a 1995 L36 deceleration-stall PCM calibration action, record 601121 a 1998 closed-throttle deceleration stall, record 617724 a 2000-2001 ignition/start-switch no-crank condition, and record 10006623 a 2004 L36 low-idle or garage-shift stall. No exact communication in the reviewed set establishes a fourteen-year CKP/ICM population, heat-soak mechanism, paired replacement practice, tachometer signature or no-code frequency.
proposal.solution: Classify the event as no-crank, crank/no-start, stall, misfire or loss of power before testing. Capture PCM, theft, ignition and network DTCs and freeze-frame data; verify battery/charging voltage, powers, grounds, spark, injector pulse, fuel pressure and live crank/cam signals under the failure condition. Test CKP circuits and the ignition module only under the applicable service chart. Do not buy a crankshaft sensor, ignition module, coils or harmonic-balancer tools from this page; engine RPO, signal loss, electrical path, part number, relearn requirement and VIN fitment must be established first.

before.title: Fuel Tank Pressure Sensor Defect — Fuel Leak and Fire Risk (NHTSA Recall 03V238000, SSEi)
before.description: Under NHTSA recall 03V238000 (GM recall 03038), the fuel tank pressure sensor on supercharged Bonneville SSEi models is unusually susceptible to malfunction; a failed sensor lets the EVAP system apply excessive vacuum during self-diagnostic testing, damaging fuel system components. Fuel can then leak from the vehicle during refueling, creating a fire hazard in the presence of an ignition source. The campaign covered roughly 102,000 GM vehicles including the Bonneville SSEi, with owner notification beginning October 17, 2003.
before.solution: Have a GM dealer replace the fuel tank pressure sensor — the recall remedy is free regardless of vehicle age. Check the VIN at recalls.nhtsa.dot.gov to confirm whether the recall was ever performed on a given car.
symptoms: Service Engine Soon light illuminated
Fuel odor or visible fuel leak when refueling
Inaccurate fuel gauge readings
Increased noise from the fuel tank area
Poor driveability

before.title: Instrument Cluster Gauge (Stepper Motor) and Backlighting Failure
before.description: The 2000-2005 Bonneville instrument cluster suffers from the same defective gauge stepper motors and failing backlighting bulbs that plague GM clusters of this era. Individual gauges — speedometer, tachometer, fuel, coolant temperature, oil, or voltage — stick, peg past maximum, read erratically, or die entirely, and the dash backlighting dims or goes dark. An entire cottage industry of mail-in rebuild services exists specifically for this cluster, confirming how widespread the failure is.
before.solution: Have the cluster rebuilt with updated X27.168-style stepper motors and new backlighting bulbs (mail-in services run about $130-$250 and preserve the odometer mileage), or replace the faulty stepper motors yourself with basic soldering skills. Used replacement clusters require mileage reprogramming, so rebuilding the original is the accepted fix.
symptoms: Speedometer or tachometer needle sticks, jumps, or pegs past maximum
Inaccurate fuel, temperature, or voltage gauge readings
One or more gauges completely dead
Dash backlighting dim or not working
Gauges sweep erratically at startup

before.title: Mass Air Flow (MAF) Sensor Contamination and Failure
before.description: The MAF sensor on OBD-II 3800-powered Bonnevilles is a frequent failure point: its hot-wire element becomes contaminated with dirt or oil (often from over-oiled aftermarket filters) or the sensor electronics fail outright, sending a low or erratic frequency signal to the PCM and setting codes P0101/P0102. The result is hesitation, stumbling, rough idle, lack of power, and stalling. A classic 3800 diagnostic trick — the engine running noticeably better with the MAF unplugged — confirms the sensor as the culprit.
before.solution: Clean the sensor element with dedicated MAF cleaner as a first step; if symptoms or codes return, replace the MAF sensor, a common and straightforward repair on these cars. Also verify the intake tube is sealed and check the MAF/O2 fuse, which feeds the sensor's 12V supply.
symptoms: Hesitation or stumble on acceleration
Stalling at idle or when coming to a stop
Check engine light with P0101/P0102
Rough idle and lack of power
Engine runs better with the MAF sensor unplugged

before.title: Plastic Upper Intake Manifold (Plenum) Degradation and Coolant Ingestion (3800 Series II)
before.description: The composite plastic upper intake manifold on the 3800 Series II V6 degrades over time, most notoriously around the hot EGR stovepipe passage, allowing coolant to leak internally into the intake runners or externally near the throttle body/thermostat area. This is a separate failure from the lower intake manifold gasket problem — the plenum material itself erodes and warps with heat cycles. Left unaddressed, coolant pooling in the intake can be drawn into the cylinders and hydrolock the engine, bending rods or destroying it outright.
before.solution: Replace the upper intake manifold with an updated unit (aftermarket versions include a reinforced/aluminum EGR sleeve) along with new gaskets; most shops replace the lower intake gaskets at the same time since access overlaps. Monitor coolant level closely and never keep driving an engine that is consuming coolant with no visible leak.
symptoms: Unexplained coolant loss with no visible puddle
White sweet-smelling exhaust smoke at startup
Rough idle or misfire, especially after sitting
Low coolant warning light
Engine cranks but will not rotate (hydrolock) in severe cases

before.title: Power Window Regulator Cable and Motor Failure
before.description: The cable-type power window regulators on 2000-2005 Bonnevilles fail repeatedly: the thin lift cable frays and snaps or a small plastic pulley/housing piece cracks, letting the cable unwind so the glass drops into the door — sometimes while driving, without the switch being touched. CarComplaints logs 64 owner complaints on the 2000 model year alone, with an average failure mileage around 90,000 and many owners reporting three or four regulator failures across different doors on the same car.
before.solution: Replace the failed regulator (and motor, which is often sold as one assembly) with an updated aftermarket unit; the door panel must come off, and owners commonly replace regulators on multiple doors over the car's life. Aftermarket assemblies are inexpensive, making this a manageable repair at an independent shop or DIY.
symptoms: Window suddenly drops into the door, even unattended
Clicking, chattering, or grinding noise when operating the window
Window moves slowly or stops mid-travel
Window off-track or tilted in the channel
Motor runs but glass does not move (snapped cable)

before.title: SSEi Supercharger Nose-Drive Coupler and Bearing Wear (Eaton M62/M90)
before.description: The Eaton roots-type supercharger on the Bonneville SSEi (M62 on 1992-1995 Series I, M90 on 1996-2003 Series II) uses a plastic isolator coupler and snout bearings that wear out with age and mileage, typically past 100,000-120,000 miles. A worn coupler produces a distinctive rattle/grind at idle that disappears when revved, while failing snout bearings produce a whine or buzz that rises with engine RPM. Continued operation eventually chews up the coupler and can damage the rotor pack or seize the snout drive.
before.solution: Rebuild the supercharger nose drive with an Eaton-spec kit (front and rear bearings, coupler, snout seal, snap ring) and refill with proper supercharger oil, or install a rebuilt snout assembly from a 3800 specialist such as ZZPerformance. This is a well-documented DIY-friendly repair on these cars.
symptoms: Rattling or grinding noise at idle that goes away when revved
Whine or buzzing noise that increases with RPM
Oil seepage from the supercharger snout
Low supercharger oil level
Reduced boost or sluggish acceleration in advanced wear

proposal.title: SSEi Supercharger Nose-Drive Coupler and Bearing Wear (Eaton M62/M90)
proposal.description: The frozen page asserts age/mileage failure of the Eaton M62/M90 coupler and snout bearings across 1992-2003 Bonneville SSEi, specific rattle/whine signatures, progression to rotor-pack damage or seizure, and specialist repair products. A complete search of 833 exact Bonneville communications found no row matching supercharger, coupler, nose-drive or snout-bearing wear. Parts-vendor and buyer-guide pages do not establish the indexed population, 100,000-120,000-mile window, root cause or fitment across both supercharger generations.
proposal.solution: Confirm the engine and supercharger RPO, reproduce the noise and localize it with safe accessory-drive and service-information procedures. Distinguish belt, tensioner, idler, alternator, water pump, supercharger coupler/backlash, snout bearing, rotor contact and other engine noise before disassembly; verify lubricant level and specification only under the correct Eaton/GM procedure. Do not buy a coupler, bearing kit, snout assembly, oil or rebuilt supercharger from this page; supercharger model, noise source, damage extent, part number and VIN fitment must be established first.
